answer: One practical mechanism is reputation grafting. A newcomer cannot transact alone; it must be grafted onto an orchard of established agents, each staking timber-weight collateral proportional to the graft. An established agent lends its good name as pigment that colors every newcomer it vouches for — and fraud stains that pigment, cutting the sponsor's own stake. Planting a thousand sybil grafts would demand a thousand real collateral locks and sponsors willing to stain their records, while an honest newcomer grafts once and grows.
